- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) mid-period, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33) — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 20% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses early correction phases — add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral within 3 days.
